glosses: Something that could happen, or could be the case, under different circumstances; a potentiality.

examples.text: When the golf ball is there, the whole self-interference package — the hopes, worries, and fears; the thoughts on how-to and how-not-to; the woulds, the coulds, and the shoulds — is there too.
Shushona you must learn to rightfully prioritize all the woulds, shoulds and coulds of your life.
Before I was blind, I could see very well.
When I was young everybody could easily find a job in a matter of days.
When I was your age, I could run 10mi in under an hour.
I could only find the street, but I couldn't locate his house.

glosses: Used as a past subjunctive (contrary to fact).

examples.text: I think he could do it if he really wanted to.
I wish I could fly!
I'd have thought you could have done the dishes, at least.

glosses: Used to politely ask for permission to do something.

examples.text: Could I borrow your coat?

glosses: Used to politely ask for someone else to do something.

examples.text: Could you proofread this email?
I wonder, you couldn't loan me the money, could you?

glosses: Used to show the possibility that something might happen.

examples.text: Even without hovering drones, a lurking assassin, a thumping score and a denouement, the real-life story of Edward Snowden, a rogue spy on the run, could be straight out of the cinema. We could rearrange the time if you like.
